table.name: circuits
table.purpose: Reference/dimension table of racing circuits (one row per circuit, 72 total) in a Formula 1 statistics database. Each row holds the circuit's unique ID, slug, name, location, country, geographic coordinates, and a Wikipedia URL. Races are linked to circuits via races.circuitId -> circuits.circuitId.

circuitId.name: circuitId
circuitId.description: Primary key; unique numeric identifier for each circuit. Referenced by races.circuitId (many races per circuit).

circuitRef.name: circuitRef
circuitRef.description: Unique short slug identifying the circuit (e.g. 'ricard', 'zolder', 'interlagos'), used as a stable textual reference key.

country.name: country
country.description: Country where the circuit is located (e.g. France, Belgium, USA).

lat.name: lat
lat.description: Geographic latitude of the circuit in decimal degrees (range -34.9 to 57.3, consistent with worldwide circuit locations).

lng.name: lng
lng.description: Geographic longitude of the circuit in decimal degrees (range -118.2 to 138.9, consistent with worldwide circuit locations).

location.name: location
location.description: Town or locality of the circuit (e.g. Le Castellet, Heusden-Zolder, Silverstone).

name.name: name
name.description: Full human-readable name of the circuit (e.g. Circuit Paul Ricard, Zolder, Silverstone Circuit).

url.name: url
url.description: Wikipedia article URL describing the circuit; unique per circuit.

table.name: constructorResults
table.purpose: Per-race championship points earned by each Formula 1 constructor (team), one row per constructor per race. This is the Ergast F1 database schema; it feeds constructorStandings. The 'status' column flags exceptional outcomes such as disqualification ('D').

constructorId.name: constructorId
constructorId.description: Foreign key to constructors.constructorId — the constructor (F1 team) this result belongs to. 172 distinct constructors, many rows per constructor.

constructorResultsId.name: constructorResultsId
constructorResultsId.description: Surrogate primary key of the table; unique across all 11,082 rows.

points.name: points
points.description: Championship points earned by the constructor in that race (aggregated over its drivers). Mostly 0 (no points), max 66; fractional values would reflect modern F1 points including fastest-lap halves.

raceId.name: raceId
raceId.description: Foreign key to races.raceId — the race this constructor result is for. Up to ~20 constructors per race.

status.name: status
status.description: Result status flag; almost always null, with the only observed value 'D' (17 rows), which in the Ergast F1 schema means the constructor was disqualified from that race. Null means a normal, valid result.

table.name: constructorStandings
table.purpose: Formula 1 constructor (team) championship standings snapshots: one row per constructor per race, showing cumulative points, championship position, and win count after that race (Ergast F1 database schema).

constructorId.name: constructorId
constructorId.description: Foreign key to constructors.constructorId; identifies the constructor (team) this standing row belongs to.

constructorStandingsId.name: constructorStandingsId
constructorStandingsId.description: Surrogate primary key uniquely identifying each constructor-standing row.

points.name: points
points.description: Constructor's cumulative championship points total as of that race (max 765, half-point values like 27.5 reflect historical F1 points systems).

position.name: position
position.description: Constructor's championship standing position (rank) after that race, 1 = leading the championship.

positionText.name: positionText
positionText.description: Text representation of the championship position; in this data it is always the same as the numeric position (in the Ergast schema it can hold 'D' for disqualified, but no such values appear here).

raceId.name: raceId
raceId.description: Foreign key to races.raceId; the race after which this standing snapshot was computed.

wins.name: wins
wins.description: Number of race wins accumulated by the constructor up to and including that race (max 19).

table.name: constructors
table.purpose: Reference/dimension table of Formula 1 constructors (racing teams) that have participated in the championship, one row per constructor, with a unique id, slug, display name, nationality, and Wikipedia link. It is the parent of results, qualifying, constructorResults, and constructorStandings via constructorId.

constructorId.name: constructor_id
constructorId.description: Primary key: unique numeric identifier for each constructor (Formula 1 racing team). Referenced by constructorResults, constructorStandings, qualifying, and results.

constructorRef.name: constructor_ref
constructorRef.description: Unique short slug/code identifying the constructor, derived from the team name (e.g. 'tyrrell', 'tec-mec', 'cooper-borgward'). Used as a stable textual reference key.

name.name: name
name.description: Full display name of the constructor (Formula 1 team), e.g. 'Alfa Romeo', 'Brabham-Repco', 'Larrousse'.

nationality.name: nationality
nationality.description: Country of origin of the constructor, e.g. British, American, Italian, French.

url.name: url
url.description: Wikipedia article URL for the constructor. Not unique (171 distinct for 208 rows) because related teams (e.g. Cooper variants) share the same article.

table.name: driverStandings
table.purpose: Formula 1 driver championship standings snapshots: one row per driver per race, showing cumulative points, championship position, and win count after that race (Ergast F1 database schema).

driverId.name: driverId
driverId.description: Foreign key to drivers.driverId — the driver this championship-standing row belongs to.

driverStandingsId.name: driverStandingsId
driverStandingsId.description: Surrogate primary key uniquely identifying each driver-standings row.

points.name: points
points.description: Cumulative championship points the driver had accumulated as of this race (max 397, e.g. a season total; half-point values like 27.5 reflect historical F1 half-point rules).

position.name: position
position.description: Driver's position in the championship standings after the given race (1 = championship leader; up to 108 for drivers with no points, ordered by tie-break rules).

positionText.name: positionText
positionText.description: Textual representation of the standings position; in this dataset it is always the same numeric value as `position` (in other F1 datasets it can hold 'D' for disqualified, but no such values appear here).

raceId.name: raceId
raceId.description: Foreign key to races.raceId — the race up to (and including) which the standings are calculated; standings are updated after each race.

wins.name: wins
wins.description: Cumulative number of race wins the driver had as of this race (max 13 in a season).

table.name: drivers
table.purpose: Reference/dimension table of racing drivers (Formula 1, per the Ergast-style schema shared with races, results, lapTimes, etc.). One row per driver who has participated in the championship, with identity, nationality, date of birth, modern driver code and permanent number, and a Wikipedia link. driverId is the primary key referenced by results, qualifying, driverStandings, lapTimes and pitStops.

code.name: driver_code
code.description: Three-letter driver code (e.g. VER, ROS, SAI) used in modern F1 timing/TV graphics; null for the vast majority of drivers because codes were only introduced in 2014. Duplicates like BIA/MAG arise because codes are unique only among active drivers.

dob.name: date_of_birth
dob.description: Driver's date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD). Range 1896-12-28 to 1998-10-29 is consistent with the full history of Formula 1 and pre-war-era racers.

driverId.name: driver_id
driverId.description: Primary key of the drivers table; unique numeric identifier for each driver. Referenced by driverStandings, lapTimes, pitStops, qualifying and results.

driverRef.name: driver_ref
driverRef.description: Unique slug-style reference identifier for the driver, typically a lowercase surname-based token (e.g. 'gilles_villeneuve', 'bonnier'); used as a stable external/API key.

forename.name: forename
forename.description: Driver's first/given name (e.g. Jo, Michael, Onofre).

nationality.name: nationality
nationality.description: Driver's nationality as an adjective (British, American, Italian, ...), including hyphenated dual nationalities like American-Italian.

number.name: permanent_number
number.description: Permanent car/race number assigned to the driver (2-99). Null for ~96% of rows because permanent driver numbers were only mandated from the 2014 season onward; before that numbers varied per race.

surname.name: surname
surname.description: Driver's family name (e.g. Bonnier, Marimón, Villeneuve).

url.name: wikipedia_url
url.description: Wikipedia article URL for the driver (URL-encoded); one row has an empty string instead of a link.

table.name: lapTimes
table.purpose: Per-lap timing data for Formula 1 races (Ergast-style schema): one row per driver per lap of a race, giving the lap time (in ms and m:ss.mmm format) and the driver's position at the end of that lap. Primary key is the composite (raceId, driverId, lap).

driverId.name: driverId
driverId.description: Foreign key to drivers.driverId — the driver who recorded the lap time.

lap.name: lap
lap.description: Lap number within the race (1 to 78; 78 laps matches the longest F1 race distance). Part of the natural key (raceId, driverId, lap).

milliseconds.name: milliseconds
milliseconds.description: Lap time in milliseconds (e.g. 91255 ms = 1:31.255). Matches the 'time' column exactly.

position.name: position
position.description: Driver's race position (1–24) at the end of that lap.

raceId.name: raceId
raceId.description: Foreign key to races.raceId — the race in which the lap was set.

time.name: time
time.description: Lap time formatted as m:ss.mmm (e.g. 1:31.255), the human-readable form of 'milliseconds'.

table.name: pitStops
table.purpose: One row per pit stop made by a driver during a race (Formula 1 data, Ergast-style schema): which race, which driver, which stop number, the lap it occurred on, the time of day, and the stop duration in seconds/milliseconds. Primary key is implicitly (raceId, driverId, stop).

driverId.name: driverId
driverId.description: Identifier of the driver making the pit stop; foreign key to drivers.driverId.

duration.name: duration
duration.description: Pit stop duration in seconds, formatted as a string with millisecond precision (e.g. '24.719'); textual counterpart of the milliseconds column.

lap.name: lap
lap.description: Lap number of the race on which the pit stop occurred (1–74).

milliseconds.name: milliseconds
milliseconds.description: Pit stop duration in milliseconds (e.g. 30888 = 30.888 s). The max of 2,011,266 ms (~33.5 min) is an outlier, likely a red-flag/very long stop.

raceId.name: raceId
raceId.description: Identifier of the race in which the pit stop took place; foreign key to races.raceId.

stop.name: stop
stop.description: Sequential number of the pit stop for that driver in that race (1st stop, 2nd stop, etc., up to 6).

time.name: time
time.description: Local clock time of day (HH:MM:SS) at which the pit stop occurred.

table.name: qualifying
table.purpose: Formula 1 qualifying session results: one row per driver per race, giving the driver's constructor, car number, final qualifying position, and best lap times in the Q1/Q2/Q3 qualifying segments (m:ss.mmm format). This is the standard Ergast F1 database 'qualifying' table.

constructorId.name: constructorId
constructorId.description: Foreign key to constructors.constructorId — the team the driver was driving for in this qualifying session.

driverId.name: driverId
driverId.description: Foreign key to drivers.driverId — the driver who recorded this qualifying result.

number.name: number
number.description: The driver's car/race number used in that session (0–99, e.g. 7, 18). Not a unique identifier; it is the number displayed on the car.

position.name: position
position.description: Final qualifying position (grid slot) the driver achieved in the session, 1 = pole sitter, up to 28.

q1.name: q1
q1.description: The driver's best lap time in qualifying segment Q1, formatted as m:ss.mmm (minutes:seconds.milliseconds). Null/empty if the driver set no Q1 time.

q2.name: q2
q2.description: The driver's best lap time in qualifying segment Q2 (m:ss.mmm). Null for ~51% of rows — drivers eliminated in Q1 (or in eras without a Q2 segment) have no time.

q3.name: q3
q3.description: The driver's best lap time in qualifying segment Q3 (m:ss.mmm). Null for ~71% of rows — only the top-ten qualifiers (or, pre-2003 formats, none) take part in Q3.

qualifyId.name: qualifyId
qualifyId.description: Primary key — unique identifier for one qualifying result (one driver in one race's qualifying session).

raceId.name: raceId
raceId.description: Foreign key to races.raceId — the race whose qualifying session this result belongs to.

table.name: races
table.purpose: One row per Formula 1 Grand Prix race (1950-2017): its season year, round number, date, start time, venue circuit, official name, and Wikipedia link. It is the central fact table referenced by results, qualifying, lap times, pit stops, and standings tables.

circuitId.name: circuitId
circuitId.description: Foreign key to circuits.circuitId identifying the circuit/venue where the race was held.

date.name: date
date.description: Date the race took place (stored as text, YYYY-MM-DD).

name.name: name
name.description: Official name of the Grand Prix event, e.g. 'British Grand Prix'.

raceId.name: raceId
raceId.description: Primary key identifying one race (a specific Grand Prix in a specific season). Referenced by results, qualifying, lapTimes, pitStops, driverStandings, constructorResults, constructorStandings.

round.name: round
round.description: Sequence number of the race within its championship season (1st round, 2nd round, etc.).

time.name: time
time.description: Scheduled local start time of the race (HH:MM:SS). Null for 75% of rows, mainly older races where start time is unknown.

url.name: url
url.description: Wikipedia article URL for this specific race.

year.name: year
year.description: Championship season year in which the race was held (1950-2017).

table.name: results
table.purpose: One row per driver per race: the finishing result of each driver–constructor entry in a Formula 1 Grand Prix (Ergast-style F1 database), including grid position, laps, finishing position, points, total/gap time, fastest-lap data, and retirement status.

constructorId.name: constructorId
constructorId.description: Foreign key to constructors.constructorId — the team the driver raced for in this race.

driverId.name: driverId
driverId.description: Foreign key to drivers.driverId — the driver who produced this race result.

fastestLap.name: fastestLap
fastestLap.description: Lap number on which the driver set their fastest lap of the race (null when not recorded, e.g. pre-1996 races or DNFs).

fastestLapSpeed.name: fastestLapSpeed
fastestLapSpeed.description: Average speed of the driver's fastest lap, in km/h (values ~89–257, typical of F1 circuit speeds).

fastestLapTime.name: fastestLapTime
fastestLapTime.description: Time of the driver's fastest lap, formatted m:ss.mmm.

grid.name: grid
grid.description: Starting grid position for the race; 0 means started from pit lane (or no grid slot).

laps.name: laps
laps.description: Number of laps completed by the driver in this race; 0 for drivers who did not start.

milliseconds.name: milliseconds
milliseconds.description: Total race time in milliseconds for classified finishers; null for non-finishers or when not recorded.

number.name: number
number.description: Car/race number used by the driver in this race.

points.name: points
points.description: Championship points scored by the driver for this result (fractional values reflect half-points for shared fastest lap under old rules).

position.name: position
position.description: Official finishing position as recorded in historical data; null when the driver was not classified (DNF/DNS/DQ).

positionOrder.name: positionOrder
positionOrder.description: Finishing position used for ordering results (always populated, 1..39, including non-finishers ordered after finishers).

positionText.name: positionText
positionText.description: Display text for the result: a number for finishers, or a code such as 'R' (retired), 'F' (not classified but running at finish), 'D' (disqualified), 'W' (withdrawn), 'E' (excluded).

raceId.name: raceId
raceId.description: Foreign key to races.raceId — the race this result belongs to.

rank.name: rank
rank.description: Rank of the driver's fastest lap within the race (1 = fastest lap of the race); null when fastest-lap data is unavailable.

resultId.name: resultId
resultId.description: Primary key — unique identifier for one driver's result in one race.

statusId.name: statusId
statusId.description: Foreign key to status.statusId — how the race ended for this driver (e.g. finished, accident, engine failure).

time.name: time
time.description: Gap to the race winner as a formatted string, e.g. '+24.160' or '+8:22.19'; null for the winner and non-finishers.

table.name: seasons
table.purpose: Lookup table of Formula One championship seasons, one row per year from 1950 to 2017, each with a link to its Wikipedia article. Likely referenced by the races table to group races by season.

url.name: url
url.description: Wikipedia article URL for that Formula One season (e.g. http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Formula_One_season). One unique URL per row, matching the year column.

year.name: year
year.description: Calendar year of the Formula One championship season. One row per season, 1950-2017 (68 consecutive years). Despite not being flagged as primary key, it is unique and acts as the table's identifier.

table.name: status
table.purpose: Lookup table of Formula 1 race result statuses: each row is a distinct race-completion classification (e.g. 'Finished', '+1 Lap') or retirement reason (e.g. 'Engine', 'Out of fuel'), identified by statusId and joined to the results table to label each race result.

status.name: status
status.description: Human-readable description of the race finish/retirement status. Values include finishing classifications expressed as laps behind the leader (e.g. '+1 Lap', '+30 Laps'), 'Finished', and retirement reasons such as 'Engine', 'Out of fuel', 'Fuel rig', 'Water pipe', 'Exhaust'. One row per distinct status.

statusId.name: statusId
statusId.description: Primary key of the status lookup table; unique identifier for each finish/retirement status. Referenced by results.statusId to classify how each driver's race ended.
